extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and policymakers interested in wartime labor, government policy, and international relief
extracted.subtask_description: A multi-topic wartime newspaper article reporting on domestic labor disputes (coal industry), government decisions (fines, wage/price policy, rationing), and international relief administration proposals. It covers facts, official statements, and procedural developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject to War Labor Board approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements on portal-to-portal pay (e.g., the $1.30 proposal) are subject to approval by the War Labor Board; board members may question or modify agreed figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public members of the board asked pointed questions suggesting the board might modify the $1.30 figure; approval is a necessary step for tentative agreements to take effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal obligation to pay travel time at time-and-a-half
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions were raised whether operators are under legal obligation to pay travel time at time-and-a-half rates (the old contract called for pay-and-a-half over 35 hours), and whether that obligation survives contract expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chairman Davis queried legal obligations; if the old contract expired, its pay provisions may not apply; if the board decides travel-time pay is due, the rate should not exceed the 40-cents-an-hour minimum under the wage-and-hour law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portal-to-portal pay calculation method
rubrics_metrics.description: The tentative $1.30 portal-to-portal pay adjustment was explained as based on an average: one hour travel time for inside men paid at pay-and-a-half ($1.50), and averaging inside and outside workers produced $1.30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wayne L. Morse criticized selecting figures 'out of the air' and indicated a preference for objective determination (e.g., by survey) of actual travel time used in calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of travel time by survey
rubrics_metrics.description: A definite determination of the actual amount of travel time should be made by survey rather than allowing parties to settle on arbitrary figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board member Morse suggested a survey to measure actual travel time, signaling an objective-measurement standard when adjudicating portal-to-portal pay disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government extension of old contract permits fines
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary Ickes declared the old coal contracts extended indefinitely pending agreement on a new contract, and under that extension the government could invoke contract penalty provisions against miners who walked out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Miners contended no contract was in force after midnight May 31; Ickes' extension enabled levying of fines for the June 1-5 absence despite the contract's formal expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Walkout fines ($1 a day) and charity provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the old contract, a penalty of $1 a day (in some areas $2) may be assessed for miners failing to work without good reason; fines collected under contracts go to selected charities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ickes announced fines would be taken out of miners' next pay envelopes; the U.M.W. condemned the fines as illegal and harmful to miners' families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of safety equipment and tools (not for piece workers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement will require operators to furnish safety equipment which they require to be used and to supply tools to men working by the day or month, but not to piece workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text notes this is generally existing policy in the mines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seventh day work and double-time rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement would provide that a man has the right to work six regular days while the company may use men who have been idle during the week when Sunday work is necessary; if the company uses men on a seventh day, double time would be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies when Sunday work can be assigned and guarantees double-time pay when men are used on a seventh day.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPA adjustments of price ceilings to offset retroactive wages
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Price Administration said necessary adjustments of price ceilings will take into account wage increases approved retroactive to April 1 to 'eliminate hardship'; increases in coal price ceilings might be called for to put tentative contracts into effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators argued price ceilings must be raised to cover retroactive costs; OPA indicated it would consider such adjustments if wage increases are approved retroactively.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPA determines gasoline ration amounts; PAW/ODT roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Petroleum Administrator for War (PAW) and other agencies may propose where rationing should occur, the Office of Price Administration (OPA) determines the amount of gasoline ration; Ickes sought authority to obtain rationing powers now exercised by OPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion emphasized divided control (PAW, ODT, OPA) causes confusion; OPA may permit seasonal residents to drive to summer homes if consumption patterns justify it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on use of subsidies to compensate for price rollbacks
rubrics_metrics.description: The Senate Banking Committee sought to restrict the use of Government subsidy funds (e.g., Commodity Credit Corporation) to compensate for price rollbacks, and reported anti-subsidy legislation prohibiting subsidies to producers, processors or manufacturers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members planned possible rewrites depending on commodities included; limits depend on breadth of the Administration's rollback program.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPA order on vegetable price rollback and expected subsidies
rubrics_metrics.description: A new OPA order was reported to direct a rollback averaging about thirty-three percent in fresh vegetable prices with no provision for subsidy; rollbacks in butter and coffee may require large subsidies (estimated $350M–$500M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extent and funding of subsidy programs were said to await further information from OPA leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of central agency for relief (UNRRA) structure and functions
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration would establish a central agency with a director general, staff including field missions, a council, a central committee, and standing/regional technical committees; it would plan, coordinate, procure and arrange distribution of food, fuel, clothing, housing, medical and other essential services for war victims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The administration would assume responsibility for meeting basic needs in liberated areas and coordinate production, transportation and distribution; the central committee (four big powers) would exercise functions between council sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Member governments to provide funds, materials, and equipment; US Congress action needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Each member government would, so far as able, provide funds, materials and equipment for relief; while the document would be an executive agreement signed by the President, Congressional legislation would be required before the United States undertook financial commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature initially limited to United and Associated Nations; other authorities might later be admitted; annual budget of the director general would be allocated among member governments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities subject to military and member-government consent/control
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities of the Relief and Rehabilitation Administration would be subject to the consent and control of military authorities and to the consent of a member government in territory where it exercised administrative authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures coordination with military governance and respect for authority of local member governments in administered territories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on foreign voluntary relief agencies operating without director general's consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign voluntary relief agencies would be forbidden to engage in activity in any area receiving relief from the administration without the consent and regulation of the director general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralized control intended to coordinate relief efforts and avoid unregulated activity in administered areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate relief obligations upon liberation
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon liberation of any area by United Nations forces, the population shall immediately receive aid and relief: food, clothing and shelter; prevention of pestilence; recovery of health; arrangements for return of prisoners and exiles; resumption of production and essential services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The administration would plan and arrange for these measures to restore health and strength and assist in rebuilding.
